messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

function.name: look_up_scientific_contributions
function.description: Look up major contributions of a particular scientist, based on their name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

contributions.description: The number of major contributions to return, defaults to 3 if not provided.

message.content:
Below is a concise “cheat‑sheet” of the most important properties of hydrogen (the element H).  
I’ve grouped them into categories so you can quickly find what you need.

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Note |
|----------|----------|----------------------|
| **Atomic / Electronic** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Valence electrons | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (protium) | 1.00794 u |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | Nuclear spin | ¹H: ½, ²H: 0, ³H: ½ |
| | Magnetic moment | ¹H: 2.7928 μN, ²H: 0, ³H: 2.9785 μN |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Covalent radius | 31 pm |
| | Van der Waals radius | 120 pm |
| | Polarizability | 0.666 ×10⁻²⁴ cm³ |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (H₂ is non‑polar) |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar heat capacity (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar conductivity | 0 S m⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar refractive index | 1.000 |
| | Standard molar magnetic susceptibility | 0.000 |
